Access Control & Gate Barriers in Abu Dhabi

Card, mobile and biometric access for people, and boom barriers, gates, road blockers and bollards for vehicles.

ScrollAbu Dhabi — India

01OverviewELV & Security Systems

Access Control & Gate Barriers

An access control system decides who gets in, where and when. We install card, mobile and PIN readers and biometric terminals with fingerprint and face recognition, all managed centrally. Turnstiles and speed gates control flow at lobbies and staff entrances. At each door we fit the hardware that makes access control work: maglocks, exit buttons, door contacts and break-glass units. Visitor management handles pre-registration, badges and host notifications, and time attendance data links to your HR and payroll systems. Our team programmes the access system in-house and integrates it with CCTV, intrusion and fire interfaces.

For vehicles, we supply and install fast-cycle boom barriers and automatic sliding and swing gates for car parks and compounds. For critical sites we add road blockers and bollards for hostile-vehicle mitigation. Guard houses can be integrated with intercom, CCTV and manual override, so officers see and control each lane. Where you need hands-free entry, barriers connect to ANPR cameras or long-range UHF readers. We have delivered swing barriers, gate barriers and ANPR for Mohamed Bin Zayed University and biometric access control for Tawazun Industrial Park.

05FAQs3 questions

Access Control & Gate Barriers: common questions

More on ELV & Security Systems
Can access control link to our HR and payroll system?

Yes. Time attendance data from card or biometric readers can be linked to your HR and payroll systems, so staff records come from the same terminals that control entry. We programme the access system in-house and agree the data link with your HR team during design.

Which barrier or gate suits our car park?

It depends on traffic, space and risk. Fast-cycle boom barriers suit busy car park lanes. Automatic sliding or swing gates suit compounds and villas. Road blockers and bollards suit critical sites that need hostile-vehicle mitigation. We confirm the right option during the site survey and risk assessment.

Can we keep our existing access control system?

Often, yes. We review the current controllers, readers and door hardware, then decide what can stay and what needs replacing. Where a legacy access control system has reached its limit, we migrate it to a current platform in stages, keeping doors secure throughout the change.
